newsitem.title: CHINA: China Eximbank details H1 97 export credits - Xinhua.
newsitem.headline: China Eximbank details H1 97 export credits - Xinhua.

text.p: The Export-Import Bank of China stepped up its support for the nation's exports in the first half of the year, approving credits of 4.82 billion yuan ($580 million) and $13.48 million, the official Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.
It gave no comparison for the period last year but it said China Eximbank president Lei Zuhua had informed a board meeting that the credits were for 58 projects.

The Eximbank had signed two agreements for a total of $65.6 million in export buyer's credits, had played a role in 125 export credit insurance deals valued at $163 million and had provided 57 export guarantees worth $427 million, the news agency said.

The bank also agreed to relend $1.5 billion in foreign government loans to finance 48 Chinese projects while it also signed five agreements calling for it to relend 280 million yuan in preferential Chinese government loans to overseas borrowers.
"Simply stated, we experienced considerable growth in the first half of this year," Lei was quoted as saying.

Bank chairman Tong Zhiguang said the Eximbank would continue to support the development of medium to large state-owned enterprises by offering funding needed to finance exports of high-tech equipment, ships, aircraft, machinery and electronic products.
The Eximbank, set up in 1994, is one of China's three state-run banks making policy-oriented loans supporting exports of capital goods.
